name: v2026.1023.0
body:
# Paperclip v2026.1023.0

> Released: 2026-10-23

Paperclip v2026.1023.0 carries 200 commits, promoted from `2026.1012.1-beta.0`. The headline is private work: a task or project can now be marked private and shared with named people and agents; everyone else cannot open it, find it in task lists or search, read its run transcripts, or reach it through a plugin. Around that: agents can run through your own model gateway (OpenRouter, Amazon Bedrock, Google Gemini, or any OpenAI Responses, Anthropic Messages, or Chat Completions endpoint), Slack bots set themselves up through Slack's Manifest API, the GitHub review bot gets a two-screen setup and a real **Paperclip Review** status check, Costs becomes an exact ledger that also shows monthly subscription fees, and connected assistants can edit tasks, upload files, and configure agents over MCP. Underneath, OpenAI Dot and Pi 1.0 join the experimental Runner, native OpenCode streams as it types, each agent gets a persistent cryptographic identity, and idle instances stop polling the database every second.

## Breaking Changes

- **Operators can now edit the company.** The Operator role preset grows from one grant (`tasks:assign`) to fourteen: agent creation and configuration, skills, environments, invitations, task assignment, pipelines, connections, tool management and use, and audit reads. Existing Operators pick up the missing grants through the normal startup seeding; custom grant scopes are kept. Join approval and member-permission management stay out of the preset, and inviting an Admin now requires join approval while inviting an Owner also requires member-permission management. Review your member roles if Operators were meant to be read-mostly. ([#15377](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15377))
- **GitHub review bots move behind their own experimental setting.** The **GitHub Code Review Bot** catalog entry, its setup, and its management screens appear only while **Settings → Experimental → GitHub review bots** (`enableGitHubReviewBots`, off by default) is on; existing bots keep running while it is off. The old setup-method and delegated-agent screens are gone, and per-person automatic-run flags are replaced by author include/exclude filters (legacy `people[].automaticReviews` values are read but ignored). ([#15416](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15416))
- **Budgets hold on unpriced usage by default.** Each budget policy gains an unpriced-usage setting that defaults to `block`: while a run's usage has no reliable price, the policy counts as at its limit until the charge is resolved through the audited cost adjustment flow. Set the policy to `allow` to keep running on unpriced usage. ([#14997](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14997))

## Highlights

- **Private tasks and projects** — Mark a task private when you create it, or make a project private with its own member list; a personal private project is created for you on first use. Private work is readable only by its responsible user, creator, current assignee, named grantees, and private-project members, and that rule applies to task lists and task counts, search, activity, run detail, transcripts, events, and logs, documents, attachments, work products, and every plugin read. Two surfaces stay company-wide on purpose: dashboard and sidebar totals may count private work without exposing a title or identifier, and the company run list shows a locked row for a private task's run with only the agent, status, timing, token, and cost fields, so budget oversight keeps working. Privacy flows down to children; sharing a child never exposes its parent or siblings. Owners and admins do not see private tasks by default and must request `?breakGlass=true`, which writes an audit row and a warning notice on the task. Agents' access is intersected with the run's responsible user, so reusing an agent does not carry another person's permissions. ([#14717](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14717), [#10633](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/10633), [#14718](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14718))
- **Bring your own model gateway** — Connectors gains rows for OpenRouter, Amazon Bedrock, Google Gemini, and generic Responses API, Messages API, Chat Completions API, and local endpoints. URLs, protocol, region, and credentials live on the connection; the agent's Harness / Runtime page picks a compatible **Connection** from a dropdown and the model picker accepts manual IDs. Codex (legacy and Runner) routes to OpenRouter or custom Responses endpoints, Claude (legacy and Runner) to OpenRouter, custom Messages endpoints, or Bedrock, and OpenCode and Hermes to OpenRouter or custom Chat Completions endpoints. OpenRouter connections without an explicit model list load OpenRouter's public catalog. ([#14970](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14970), [#15341](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15341))
- **Slack bots set themselves up** — New Slack bot drafts default to automatic setup: paste a temporary App configuration token, Paperclip creates the app through Slack's Manifest API, installs it through OAuth, links your Slack account, uploads the agent's avatar, and verifies delivery in a four-screen wizard with no Slack CLI involved ([#15413](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15413)). A new **Require at-mention** setting stops thread replies from waking the agent without an explicit mention ([#15612](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15612)); a follow-up sent after a Slack Stop starts a fresh turn instead of stalling ([#15737](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15737)); and Slack agents now know the saved slash command people use to link their accounts, link every task they create, and report results and review requests back in the originating thread ([#15576](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15576), [#15579](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15579), [#15611](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15611)).
- **A two-screen GitHub review bot** — Setup is now Choose agent, then Connect GitHub under a personal account or organization; GitHub asks for creation and installation consent, and Paperclip stores the App secrets locally, imports repository access, and verifies delivery. Each accepted request gets one editable App-owned progress comment, and review assessments publish a **Paperclip Review** check for the reviewed commit with a configurable passing score (1–5) that branch protection can require. A self-hosted instance needs one Paperclip Cloud approval before its first managed GitHub connection, because Cloud hosts the fixed OAuth callback and signed webhook inbox; tokens are sealed to your instance. ([#15416](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15416))
- **Costs you can reconcile** — Accounting is now a durable, exact ledger: usage receipts are fsynced and replayed after failures, retries settle one charge, amounts keep decimal cents, and every event is marked reported, estimated, or unpriced instead of silently zero ([#14991](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14991), [#14997](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14997)). The Costs page reports each connected ChatGPT or Claude subscription's monthly fee once beside API spend, lets you enter the real price, and keeps ambiguous plans unpriced ([#15634](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15634)); quota reads are scoped to authorized company accounts ([#14994](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14994)); cost gaps are listed by agent with links to the affected runs, the model the runtime actually selected is recorded, and a retry appears only when saved evidence is ready ([#15948](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15948)); and historical pricing gaps show as a neutral note under the totals rather than a red error ([#15459](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15459)).
- **Assistants that can do more over MCP** — A connected Claude Code, Codex, or other MCP assistant can now edit tasks, finish or block them, write documents and revisions, register deliverables, upload files through expiring tickets, and, with a separately consented configuration scope, manage agent settings and instructions, projects and repositories, and skills ([#15380](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15380)). Connections are named by owner and client ("Dotta's Codex connection") with the authorizing person's avatar, revoked rows disappear, and the copied invitation is shorter ([#15411](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15411)).
- **Sixteen more apps in the catalog** — Gauge ([#15596](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15596)), Superagent ([#15394](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15394)), Telem.AI web search ([#15379](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15379)), Enterpret ([#13906](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/13906)), Calendly, Exa, Firecrawl, GSC Wizard, Parallel Search, Tavily, and Windsor.ai ([#15621](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15621)), and Bitly, Context7, Hugging Face, and Resend ([#15686](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15686)) join as verified hosted MCP connections. Sentry sign-in discovers OAuth through its MCP resource metadata, so setup no longer asks for a client ID and secret ([#15837](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15837)), and OAuth grants now record whether each scope came from the provider or from Paperclip's request ([#14059](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14059)).
- **New Runner providers** — OpenAI Dot joins as a standalone experimental agent choice: pair your Dot with a one-use code, and the Runner delivers assignments over MCP Events while Dot uses its own tools and reports back ([#15402](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15402), [#15414](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15414), [#15581](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15581), [#15734](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15734)). Pi 1.0 runs through the experimental Runner with explicit provider and model selection ([#14921](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14921)), and the Cursor Runner integration is consolidated onto mainline recovery behavior with a public install path ([#15075](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15075)).
- **Codex and OpenCode that just start** — Native Codex uses the installed Codex CLI and accepts usable older or newer versions, so a clean npm install no longer needs a global command ([#15555](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15555)); a model that the sandbox's Codex CLI is too old for is swapped for a compatible one with a visible warning instead of failing every turn ([#15399](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15399), [#15519](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15519)); saved runs survive server upgrades ([#15518](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15518)); and task environment variables reach later turns and tool commands ([#15451](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15451)). Native OpenCode streams text as it arrives ([#15708](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15708)), starts without the postinstall script that package managers skip ([#15702](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15702)), and selects the bundled Linux assets for remote runs without path overrides ([#15721](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15721)).
- **Reports you can open on the task** — HTML attachments and workspace `.html` files render in an opaque-origin sandbox with view-source and download controls ([#15447](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15447)), and CSV files open as tables with row numbers, sticky headers, and record counts ([#15445](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15445)).
- **Clearer task provenance and waits** — A follow-up task an agent creates while working on a task now defaults to that task as its parent, and the task page shows "Created from <task> by <agent>" ([#15762](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15762)); native agents can schedule their own one-shot task monitor and yield until it fires ([#15446](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15446)); the monitor card gets an X with a confirmation ([#15735](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15735)); and a saved pull request stays visible in Properties with its review request and a **Check status** action even when the provider lookup fails ([#15375](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15375)).
- **Your primary agent** — Each person gets one primary agent per company, shown with a crown on the roster and used as the fallback for new tasks and Chat when there is no recent choice; the first agent you create becomes primary automatically and can be changed on the agent profile ([#15470](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15470)).
- **Company decision models and fast responses** — Company Settings can bind one shared OpenAI or OpenRouter API connection for small typed model decisions, with permission checks, budget reservations, and a Costs → Decisions history ([#15473](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15473)). On top of it, **Experimental fast responses** posts a short acknowledgement comment within three seconds of a human message while the agent starts its normal run, in tasks, Agent Chat, and Slack and GitHub threads ([#15748](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15748)).

## Fixes

- **Workspaces and sandboxes** — A transient sandbox copy-back failure is retried up to three times before the task is held for repair, and remaining holds explain what happened in plain language ([#15920](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15920)); a remote sandbox whose required copy-back failed is kept, with its files, behind an explicit repair decision instead of being deleted by cleanup ([#15479](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15479), [#15790](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15790)); server shutdown waits for a legacy adapter's workspace export before releasing its sandbox lease ([#15857](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15857)); a reused saved worktree keeps its original repository when project settings change ([#15528](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15528)); an accepted native result is no longer mistaken for lost work by the orphan reaper after a restart ([#15718](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15718)); OpenCode runs in the realized workspace via `--dir` ([#11438](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/11438)); Daytona OpenCode sessions keep their deadlines ([#15905](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15905)); and OpenCode timeouts no longer claim the configured deadline expired ([#15789](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15789)).
- **Runs, recovery, and questions** — A retry no longer burns itself while a stopped run's environment is still cleaning up, and settled repair instructions stop reappearing in later wakes ([#15463](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15463)); a review wait whose automatic repair also leaves no wake path now records a board decision instead of sitting silently ([#15764](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15764)); a parent is woken again when a child finishes requested revisions ([#15372](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15372)); native runs resume cleanly after connection approval decisions with final usage retained ([#15471](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15471), [#15420](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15420), [#15514](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15514)); a pending tool request expires on its own when the user has already connected the service in Apps ([#15856](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15856)); agents stop re-asking questions that moved into feed history ([#15392](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15392)); archiving a task during its completion no longer deadlocks ([#15615](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15615)); and a task policy with a monitor but no stages no longer crashes the task page ([#15593](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15593)).
- **Adapters** — Claude CLI sessions resume across per-run agent file copies ([#15437](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15437)); Hermes gets managed instructions through its system overlay instead of a copy in every resumed user turn ([#15439](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15439)); and external agents such as Dot are told to use their own tools when a Paperclip app is missing ([#15734](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15734)).
- **Connections and MCP** — One oversized or malformed MCP reply fails only that call instead of locking the whole connection in an error state ([#15462](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15462)); remote MCP callbacks keep an explicitly saved empty agent selection, token exchange sends `Accept: application/json`, and saved hidden-provider drafts resume from Finish setup ([#15686](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15686)); Airtable, Calendly, and other verified providers get the registration and form fixes found in live testing ([#15621](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15621)); and the sidebar keeps its last plugin items quiet when the server is unreachable ([#15588](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15588)).

## Improvements

- Hiring, approval, pause, resume, and termination run through a durable agent lifecycle with explicit states: proposed hires stay pending until approval, approved hires are prepared and have their harness configuration verified before work, required plugins get callbacks at each step, and the agent page shows lifecycle progress with a retry action ([#15631](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15631), [#15391](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15391)); plugins can consume a durable resource lifecycle journal with acknowledgments, seeded with a one-time baseline of existing agents and projects, and project archive and restore now write journal events ([#15343](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15343), [#15371](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15371)).
- Every agent gets a persistent Ed25519 keypair, created on hire or on its next managed run, encrypted at rest and handed to managed processes as `PAPERCLIP_AGENT_KEY_ID`, `PAPERCLIP_AGENT_PUBLIC_KEY`, and `PAPERCLIP_AGENT_PRIVATE_KEY`; the public key appears on the agent overview ([#15352](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15352)).
- Agents can file complaints and suggestions about their tooling into the instance's `agent_commentary` table through new `complain` and `suggestion-box` skills or native `submit_complaint` and `submit_suggestion` tools, keeping that feedback out of task threads ([#15367](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15367)).
- Idle instances go quiet: chat delivery, provider action, Slack sync, email, Browser Use cleanup, and five server delivery queues now wake from committed writes and known deadlines instead of scanning the database every second or three ([#15625](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15625), [#15750](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15750), [#15757](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15757), [#15802](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15802), [#15808](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15808), [#15822](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15822)); hosts that park idle instances get an idle-sleep safety report that fences accepted work, drains plugin workers, and treats finished logins, consumed retries, and verified delivery history as history rather than pending work ([#15522](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15522), [#15599](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15599), [#15761](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15761), [#15851](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15851), [#15897](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15897), [#15907](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15907)), with an opt-in final backup checkpoint before sleep ([#15629](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15629)).
- Task notifications show the actor's name and avatar and hide your own actions ([#15695](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15695)); other people's comments in task chat appear on the left with their name and avatar, and only yours are on the right in blue ([#15494](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15494)); an agent blocked by an AI connection its responsible user cannot use shows an expanded error naming the agent and connection with a link to its AI settings ([#15741](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15741)); and a teammate without the agent's required personal AI account can connect their own from inside the chat and resume the message ([#15376](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15376)).
- The task composer keeps its model label steady while the effort slider moves and the slider is larger ([#15444](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15444)), nested selectors scroll with the wheel and touch ([#15374](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15374)), the project picker always offers **No project** ([#15382](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15382)), routine descriptions keep code-block pastes in the code block and gain a copy control ([#15773](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15773)), confirmation cards stack the prompt above the target pill and hide unlabeled machine keys ([#15895](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15895)), chat connection and recovery cards share one surface ([#15771](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15771)), the Slack chat-or-tools chooser gets icons ([#15574](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15574)), the Workspace filter leaves the task and inbox filter menus ([#15788](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15788)), and the star and leave buttons leave the agent index ([#15400](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15400)).
- Tasks whose starting branch does not exist in the repository show a branch repair card that offers the remote's default branch or a typed branch and retries through the normal admission gates ([#15726](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15726)); a GitHub reference the instance's credentials cannot see is reported as inaccessible and re-checked instead of frozen as "Not found" ([#15906](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15906)); and the Paperclip skill ships its own issue-update helper and honors a harness checkout instead of demanding a second one ([#15554](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15554), [#15548](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15548)).
- Workspace jobs that exit non-zero return `422 workspace_job_failed` with the job's own output instead of a 500 ([#15941](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15941)); custom source launchers get the native Runner WebSocket transport from the shared HTTP server constructor ([#15682](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15682)); a refused local Hermes Gateway connection explains which host to check ([#15520](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15520)); and pi-local's unavailable-model error no longer dumps the model catalog ([#13628](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/13628)).
- Failure reports carry bounded evidence for Daytona acquisition timeouts and provider state, workspace base-ref resolution, sandbox transfer and sync-out errors, orphan process loss, ACP bridge terminal frames, Git worktree inspection, and stackless browser rejections ([#15946](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15946), [#15736](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15736), [#15719](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15719), [#15637](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15637), [#15481](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15481), [#15475](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15475), [#15478](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15478), [#15525](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15525), [#15940](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15940)), while proven configuration blockers such as a missing user secret, an unchosen AI account, a credential not shared with the responsible user, a local-directory project with a worktree policy, or an external service outage stay out of Sentry ([#15472](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15472), [#15618](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15618), [#15714](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15714), [#15521](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15521), [#15590](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15590)).

## Upgrade Guide

- **Migrations `0306`–`0333`** run on upgrade: `0306` allows `google` in the AI account-default provider checks; `0307` rewrites the lifecycle-event action constraint; `0308` adds `agent_identity_keys`; `0309` adds `plugin_lifecycle_acknowledgments`, indexes the lifecycle journal, and seeds a one-time baseline event per existing agent and project; `0310` adds `agent_commentary`; `0311` adds MCP attachment upload and file ticket tables; `0312` adds accounting receipt, reservation, adjustment, invoice, and provider snapshot tables, widens cost columns to `numeric`, and adds the budget unpriced-usage policy (default `block`); `0313` adds `issue_access_grants` and `project_access_members`, adds `visibility` to tasks and projects (default `open`), and backfills privacy parent edges and run bindings in 1,000-row batches; `0314` binds historical inline draft images to their first task; `0315` adds `user_company_preferences` and backfills a primary agent from history; `0316` adds decision model tables; `0317` adds OpenAI Dot binding, mailbox, and assignment tables; `0318` adds `chat_slack_registrations`; `0319` makes Dot agent refresh tokens non-expiring; `0320` adds agent lifecycle columns and derives `lifecycle_state` from each agent's current status; `0321` adds `chat_endpoints.require_at_mention`; `0322` adds AI subscription account and price tables; `0323` adds GitHub registration owner columns; `0324`–`0330` add the experimental voice session tables; `0331` adds fast-response tables and `issue_comments.origin`; `0332` adds a question-history index concurrently; `0333` adds cost data-quality indexes. `0313` and `0314` run outside a single transaction and commit each batch, so an interrupted upgrade leaves them pending and safe to rerun; expect them to take longer on instances with large run histories.
- **New environment variables**, none required: `PAPERCLIP_ISSUE_PRIVACY_MODE` (default `enforce`; `shadow` logs would-deny decisions without enforcing, `off` disables the predicate) ([#10633](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/10633)); `PAPERCLIP_DB_BACKUP_IDLE_CHECKPOINT_ENABLED=1` opts an instance with automatic backups into taking a final verified backup before idle sleep (off by default) ([#15629](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15629)); `PAPERCLIP_RESPONSIBLE_USER_AUTHZ_CACHE_TTL_MS` bounds the responsible-user permission snapshot (default `5000`) ([#10633](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/10633)).
- **New experimental settings**, all off by default: **GitHub review bots** (`enableGitHubReviewBots`) shows GitHub bot setup and management ([#15416](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15416)); **OpenAI Dot** (`enableOpenAiDot`) adds Dot as an agent choice and requires **Assistant connections (MCP)**, authenticated sign-in, and an HTTPS `PAPERCLIP_PUBLIC_URL` ([#15414](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15414)); **Experimental fast responses** (`enableFastResponses`) reveals Company Settings → Connections and allows acknowledgement comments ([#15748](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15748)). Decision model setup lives under Company Settings → General until fast responses are on ([#15473](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15473)).
- **Review Operator members** ([#15377](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15377)): Operators now hold company editing, invitation, connection, tool, and audit grants after startup seeding. Demote members who should not configure agents or connect accounts.
- **Budget policies and unpriced usage** ([#14997](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14997)): existing policies get `unpricedUsagePolicy: block`. If your agents run on providers whose prices Paperclip cannot determine, set the policy to `allow` or resolve unpriced events through the cost adjustment flow so the budget does not hold them.
- **Custom adapters and managed processes** ([#15352](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15352)): managed runs now receive `PAPERCLIP_AGENT_KEY_ID`, `PAPERCLIP_AGENT_PUBLIC_KEY`, and `PAPERCLIP_AGENT_PRIVATE_KEY`; the key values are multiline PEM strings and the private key must not be logged. The wrapping key is `PAPERCLIP_SECRETS_MASTER_KEY` or the local secrets master-key file; a wrong master key fails the run rather than regenerating the keypair.
- **Private-task callers** ([#10633](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/10633)): direct reads of a private task by a non-member return `404`; owners and admins must pass `?breakGlass=true` for an audited emergency read; plugins are non-member principals and see no private content.
- **Slack and GitHub drafts**: existing Slack bot drafts without a saved setup method stay on manual setup ([#15413](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15413)); existing GitHub bots, direct webhooks, and manual existing-App recovery keep working, but their settings are hidden until **GitHub review bots** is enabled ([#15416](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15416)).
- **Harness pins** are unchanged for Codex, Claude, and OpenCode. Native Codex now prefers the Codex CLI installed with the server package and tolerates version drift; a sandbox image whose Codex CLI is too old for the selected model is switched to a compatible model with a warning ([#15555](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15555), [#15519](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15519)).
- No other configuration or API changes require action.

## Contributors

This release has 200 commits from 7 contributors. Thank you to everyone who contributed to this release!

@lorenzozanee, @lusoris

# Paperclip v2026.1012.0

> Released: 2026-10-12

Paperclip v2026.1012.0 carries 130 commits, promoted from `2026.1006.0-beta.0`. The headline is that outside assistants can now join your team: Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, and any MCP client can connect to Paperclip as a signed-in person, review work, and delegate tasks, all behind an experimental setting. Around that: Chat leads the navigation with each agent's tasks and artifacts beside the conversation, the Connections catalog pulls in accounts you already linked in Composio and Arcade, connections carry usage instructions that reach your agents automatically, Claude Sonnet 5.5 and GPT-6.1 Sol arrive with refreshed harnesses, and agents can safely update company skills. Underneath, Codex runs survive server restarts and model-capacity errors, workspace restore locks move to crash-safe SQLite file locks, and default agent instructions shrink to a fraction of their former size.

## Breaking Changes

- **Workspace restore locks change protocol; stop every old process before upgrading.** Restore and agent-file collection locks are now OS-backed SQLite file locks under `<instance root>/locks/directory-merge/`, released by the kernel when a process crashes. Old and new versions must not write to the same instance root at once: drain and stop all old server and worker processes (including other hosts or containers) before upgrading or rolling back, then move any leftover legacy `<hash>.lock/` directories to a scratch location. Never delete or move the new `.lock.sqlite` files. See `doc/workspace-restore-locks.md`. ([#14869](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14869))
- **Stored tool grants are enforced as written.** A grant whose `scope.allow` list does not match a tool, connection, or application no longer falls through to a broader policy; grants with unknown selectors or malformed restrictions now deny access. Review custom grants after upgrading if an agent loses a tool it previously used. ([#14915](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14915))

## Highlights

- **Assistants join your team over MCP** — A new "Assistant Connection (MCP)" card in Connections lets Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, and generic MCP clients connect to Paperclip through browser OAuth or device-code consent and act as the signed-in user: read and search tasks, create and delegate work, leave human comments, read documents and deliverables, and follow results through signed event webhooks ([#14846](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14846)). Consent shows the client and organization, write access can be opted out, requests can be pinned to one company, and a `paperclip mcp` CLI device login bridges local stdio clients; it is off by default behind Settings → Experimental → "Assistant connections (MCP)" and requires an HTTPS `PAPERCLIP_PUBLIC_URL` ([#14933](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14933)).
- **Chat leads the way** — With Agent Chat enabled in the streamlined UI (the default shell), Chat is the first row in the Work navigation, the chat rail lists every eligible agent, and the side panel shows that agent's recent tasks and artifacts; a new experimental "Combined Inbox + Task List" setting folds Inbox into Tasks as views ([#15100](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15100)). Instances that switched "Streamlined UI" off keep the legacy navigation and do not see these changes. The Chat entry reopens the last conversation you visited ([#14848](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14848)), and the chat header shows the agent's avatar ([#14726](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14726)).
- **One catalog for every account** — The Connections Apps catalog discovers accounts already connected upstream in Composio, Arcade, and supported Executor gateways and groups them with native accounts under one app card, with source chips, search, and pagination ([#15254](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15254)). AgentMail is a default connection with inline setup cards in Agent Chat ([#14772](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14772)), Neon joins the catalog with OAuth or API-key sign-in ([#14980](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14980)), Asana works again with a default "Sign in with Asana" ([#14756](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14756)), and AI accounts gain a "Check usage" action that reads current provider limits for Codex, Claude, Grok, and OpenRouter ([#14936](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14936)).
- **Connections carry instructions for agents** — A connection can hold editable usage instructions that are delivered to every authorized agent turn across the native runner, legacy adapters, and HTTP/process contracts. Honcho, Mem0, Zep, Supermemory, and Cognee ship defaults, the editor appears in setup and the Permissions panel, and agent Instructions show a read-only "From connections" section ([#15216](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15216)).
- **New models, refreshed harnesses** — Claude Sonnet 5.5 is selectable for Claude Code agents with Low through Max effort, and the qualified Claude runtime moves to Claude Code 2.1.286 ([#14993](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14993)); GPT-6.1 Sol joins the Codex adapter with Fast mode and Ultra effort, Bedrock gains Sonnet 5.5, and the shared pins move to Codex 0.160.0 and OpenCode 1.18.34 ([#14942](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14942)). Claude and Codex model menus now list models in the same order as the Claude and ChatGPT apps ([#14917](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14917), [#14918](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14918)).
- **Agents maintain company skills** — Native-runner agents get an `update_skill` tool that rewrites a company skill with version checking and safe retries, recorded in version history and the audit log; the skill file API gains optional `expectedVersionId` and `idempotencyKey` fields ([#15049](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15049)). Newly created agents receive a default set of configuration grants so they can finish agent, tool, skill, and task setup without manual permission work ([#15283](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15283)).
- **Codex runs that survive restarts and capacity limits** — A native Codex turn killed by a server restart resumes in the same conversation once the old process is proven gone ([#15297](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15297)); a model at capacity shows a "Model at capacity" card and retries automatically after one and then two minutes ([#15347](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15347)); a model the ChatGPT account cannot use shows "Model unavailable" with guidance instead of generic recovery ([#15299](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15299), [#15304](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15304)); and Codex keeps its stock base prompt, receiving Paperclip's context as additive developer instructions ([#14920](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14920)).
- **A rebuilt New task dialog** — The dialog is built on the shared task composer with a Project and Worktrees bar, remembered assignee, project, and effort, and task mentions in suggestions; the status, reviewer, approver, and watchdog controls move out of the dialog into task properties, and new tasks default to the last assignee used ([#15091](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15091)). Tasks created without a title get a clean plain-text provisional title ([#15047](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15047)).
- **Far shorter default instructions** — New companies and hires get role descriptions instead of procedural manuals: the default CEO instructions drop from roughly 1,900 words to 20 ([#14985](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14985)), new non-CEO hires receive a one-sentence default manual ([#14948](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14948)), and the bundled planning skills shrink to about 400 words combined and no longer force a child-task matrix ([#15296](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15296)). Existing saved manuals and custom bundles are unchanged.

## Fixes

- **Native runner and sessions** — A run whose final answer was saved but whose shutdown failed reaches its correct final status, and the agent `list_projects` tool returns paged summaries instead of overflowing the command limit ([#15217](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15217)); tasks stopped during native preparation on an older build regain Retry and accept new messages ([#15020](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15020), [#15022](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15022)); a continuation cancelled by the queued-run review gate is treated as a review wait instead of an unknown-execution hold ([#15024](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15024)); Retry and saved-message recovery work on `SQL_ASCII` databases ([#15033](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15033)); a user-continued legacy run that times out can be retried automatically ([#14987](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14987)); a completed run no longer reports "Run failed" when instruction-file cleanup times out afterward ([#14945](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14945)) and that cleanup no longer blocks lease release ([#14866](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14866)); `write_document` and other semantic tool calls no longer fail when a document merely discusses credentials ([#14937](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14937)) or contains credential-looking text ([#15301](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15301)); long connected MCP tool names are aliased to fit provider limits and the recovery notice explains why a run was cancelled with a Continue option ([#14951](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14951)); agents keep their task context when a tool connection changes mid-task ([#14963](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14963)); native MCP gateways reject run tokens from any agent other than their owner ([#14914](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14914)); and the Codex runner's "ignored unrelated provider information" warnings stay in the run log instead of the chat ([#14929](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14929)).
- **Sandboxes and workspaces** — Sandbox runs no longer fail with `workspace_restore_failed` after an agent rebases or amends its branch ([#15268](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15268)); the Daytona driver recovers output from a log socket that goes silent ([#14889](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14889)); bridge control commands are capped at 30 seconds and active runs are flagged as suspicious after 5 minutes of silence and critical after 15 ([#14979](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14979)); multi-repository projects round-trip commits on SSH execution environments ([#14782](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14782)); isolated-worktree tasks on the Paperclip repository itself set up without a local seed config ([#14810](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14810)); and the standard Docker image bundles the remote provider pack so remote OpenCode and ACPX runs no longer fail with `runner_remote_provider_artifact_incompatible` ([#14854](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14854)).
- **Chat and task UI** — Steer and Interrupt show your message immediately and deliver to the active run even after a model or effort change, and a stopped native startup offers Retry ([#15015](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15015)); a message sent after a failed native run no longer hangs and is delivered exactly once ([#14857](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14857)); stale "Run failed", "Stopped", and "Waiting to resume" markers disappear once a later attempt supersedes them ([#14874](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14874)); dismissed agent questions stay in the task feed and remain answerable ([#15229](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15229)); confirmation cards show "Preparing approval…" until the source workspace is ready instead of erroring on click ([#14893](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14893)); an unsaved Agent Chat no longer polls the browser panel with a draft id every three seconds ([#15298](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15298)); the thread no longer calls a stale send or cancel action ([#14863](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14863)); mobile task pages get an opaque footer, steadier scrolling, a full-height document panel, and in-place document links ([#15228](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15228)) with new output staying above the composer ([#15282](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15282)); the completed-work caret sits beside its label ([#15048](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15048)), composer labels use the available width ([#15050](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15050)), branch artifacts without a remote link say so ([#15051](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15051)), the Dashboard shows each task once ([#14847](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14847)), and a selected saved subscription can be used without clicking the provider tile ([#14996](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14996)).
- **Connections and access** — Agent settings can reconnect an unavailable personal AI account in place, and a newly connected account becomes the user's default ([#14916](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14916)); generic MCP OAuth requests `offline_access` when offered so access survives token expiry ([#14950](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14950)); MCP tool discovery uses a fraction of the memory and queries on large catalogs, bounds concurrent listings with a `tool_discovery_busy` 503 under load, and answers GET on stateless endpoints with 405 ([#14864](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14864)); low-trust agents can create self-assigned work inside their permitted scope and update their own managed `AGENTS.md` from the owner's chat ([#14870](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14870)) and accept their owner's direct messages and human-assigned tasks outside an intake boundary ([#14775](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14775)); company skill imports from a server-managed project checkout no longer fail with `skill_workspace_boundary_denied` ([#10329](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/10329)); and the managed `git`/`gh` launcher retries a failed credential broker request before continuing without managed credentials ([#14856](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14856)).
- **Server resilience** — Dashboard reads ([#14873](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14873)), scoped read queries ([#15248](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15248)), and the task run list ([#15300](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15300)) retry transient PostgreSQL disconnects instead of failing the request, and routine routes return 404 for malformed ids instead of a database error ([#15313](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15313)).

## Improvements

- Experimental AI connection pools rotate new tasks across saved AI accounts while each task stays pinned to its account, behind the default-off `enableAiConnectionRouters` setting and a router plugin ([#14967](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14967)); the exe.dev sandbox provider can clone a prepared "Source VM" instead of creating a bare one ([#14975](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14975)); the native runner daemon accepts any `--listen-port` so several listening runners can share a host ([#15353](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15353)); the server keeps a durable lifecycle journal of agent hire, pause, resume, and terminate events and project create and update events as groundwork for plugin hooks ([#15280](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15280), [#15306](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15306)); Slack, GitHub, MCP, invitation, routine, and handoff prompts share one animated "copy prompt" control ([#14862](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14862)) and the Slack setup prompt matches the current flow ([#14965](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14965)); the per-action Test dialog renders MCP results as readable tables and cards ([#14859](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14859)); agents can create question cards from a single canonical question set ([#14946](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14946)) and receive identical completion-tool guidance across Codex, Claude, and OpenCode ([#14961](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14961)) with less repeated procedure text and a canonical link from `write_document` ([#15151](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15151)); and failed restores and Stop timeouts record which stage failed and why in run results and Sentry context ([#15005](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15005), [#15291](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15291), [#14990](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14990), [#14986](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14986)).

## Upgrade Guide

- **Migrations `0294`–`0305`** run on upgrade: `0294` adds a `tool_mcp_gateway_tokens` expiry index; `0295` and `0296` add aggregator account snapshot and sync tables; `0297` adds `resource_lifecycle_events` and `0300` rewrites its action check constraint; `0298` adds `tool_connections.agent_instructions` and backfills default instructions for existing Honcho, Mem0, Zep, Supermemory, and Cognee connections; `0299` adds AI connection pool, router cursor, and task pin tables plus `company_secrets.ai_session_epoch`; `0301`–`0305` add the public MCP OAuth client, grant, token, receipt, event subscription, device-flow, and admission tables. All are additive; `0298` is the only one that updates existing rows.
- **Stop all old processes before upgrading** ([#14869](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14869)): the new SQLite restore-lock protocol cannot coexist with the old directory locks. Drain every server and worker that writes to the instance root, move leftover legacy `<hash>.lock/` directories out of `<instance root>/locks/directory-merge/`, then start the new version. The same applies to rollback.
- **Review custom tool grants** ([#14915](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14915)): grants with unknown scope selectors or malformed restrictions now deny instead of falling through.
- **New experimental settings**, all off by default: "Assistant connections (MCP)" (`enablePublicMcp`) exposes the public MCP endpoint and requires `PAPERCLIP_PUBLIC_URL` to be an HTTPS origin ([#14933](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14933)); "Combined Inbox + Task List" (`enableCombinedInboxTasks`) folds Inbox into Tasks and takes effect only while "Streamlined UI" is on ([#15100](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15100)); `enableAiConnectionRouters` turns on connection pools and has no UI toggle ([#14967](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14967)).
- **Connection instructions for custom adapters** ([#15216](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15216)): HTTP adapters receive a top-level `connectionInstructions` field in the request body, either a `{ text, digest }` object or `null` when no instructions apply; process adapters receive `PAPERCLIP_CONNECTION_INSTRUCTIONS_FILE`, the path to a private JSON file holding the same `{ text, digest }` object, and the variable is set to an empty string (not a path) when no instructions apply. Adapters should append the object's `text` to the model prompt rather than passing the object through. Built-in harnesses need no change.
- **Harness pins moved** to Codex 0.160.0, Claude Agent SDK 0.3.286 (Claude Code 2.1.286), and OpenCode 1.18.34 ([#14942](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14942), [#14993](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14993)). Custom sandbox images built with Claude Code older than 2.1.284 must be rebuilt before Sonnet 5.5 works on the CLI path, and the controller and runner should be deployed before promoting a sandbox image with the new pins; remote Codex now accepts 0.149.0 up to but excluding 0.161.0.
- **New defaults**: newly created standard agents receive default configuration grants, while existing agents are unchanged ([#15283](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15283)); the runner's `--listen-port` still defaults to 43127 ([#15353](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15353)); silent active runs are flagged after 5 and 15 minutes instead of 1 and 4 hours, with no automatic cancellation ([#14979](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14979)).
- No other configuration or API changes require action.

## Contributors

This release has 130 commits from 9 contributors. Thank you to everyone who contributed to this release!

@baozdemir, @valentinpalkovic, @abderbejaoui

body:
# Paperclip v2026.1005.0

> Released: 2026-10-05

Paperclip v2026.1005.0 carries 179 commits, promoted from `2026.1002.0-beta.0`. The headline is agents that carry more with them: Grok Build runs on the native runner, agents keep their own files across tasks, company skills sync from GitHub repositories, and Browser Use Cloud gives agents a live browser that people can watch and take over from the task. Around those: most connectors now set up in one click with MCP aggregators on by default, Slack conversations round-trip between the board and the thread, Agent Chat gets its own navigation and hands finished work back to the conversation, and the task composer picks model and effort per message. Underneath, a long reliability pass hardens the native runner, sandbox transport, and the heartbeat scheduler, including a fix for a server crash loop caused by a permanently rejected queued run.

## Breaking Changes

- **Operator UI snippet injection is removed.** The `PAPERCLIP_CLOUD_UI_SNIPPET` and `PAPERCLIP_CLOUD_UI_SNIPPET_B64` settings no longer inject HTML into static or development pages. Operators who relied on them should move the integration to a plugin UI contribution before upgrading. ([#13789](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/13789))
- **Keyboard shortcuts are always on, and their settings are gone.** The instance-wide General toggle and the per-user Profile preference are both removed, along with the `GET`/`PATCH /api/auth/preferences` routes; `PATCH /api/instance/settings/general` no longer accepts `keyboardShortcuts`. Every signed-in user now has shortcuts enabled. ([#14141](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14141), [#14643](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14643))
- **@-mentioning an agent no longer starts a run.** Mentions in task comments are kept as context for the assignee; only explicit assignment and review requests start work. Workflows that used a mention to pull a second agent onto a task must assign or request review instead. ([#14577](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14577))

## Highlights

- **Grok Build on the native runner** — Grok Build joins the Paperclip Runner through ACP for both local and Daytona execution, with separate subscription-login and API-key credential paths and governed tools ([#13882](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/13882)); it ships in public installs with sandbox-owned binaries rather than a download at install time ([#14024](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14024)). The shared harness runtimes move to Codex 0.156.0, Claude Agent SDK 0.3.280, and OpenCode 1.18.32 ([#13838](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/13838)), model catalogs and reasoning controls are refreshed across the Claude, Codex, Grok, Gemini, Cursor, Kimi, and OpenCode adapters ([#13829](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/13829)), and remote native Codex accepts compatible releases from 0.149.0 instead of one exact pin ([#13853](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/13853)).
- **Agents keep their own files** — An agent's directory (AGENTS.md and its supporting files) now persists across tasks and sessions and is shared with the Instructions Editor; concurrent runs apply only the files they changed, and new saves no longer create revision history ([#14420](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14420)), on top of a new plain-directory sync transport with conflict preflight ([#14416](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14416)). Warm native Codex sessions survive managed-file collection by checkpointing only changed files after each turn ([#14735](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14735)).
- **Skills synced from GitHub** — Skills gains a Sources tab: pick a repository through an existing GitHub connection, choose which skill folders to import, and refresh on demand. Installed snapshots mean agents never fetch GitHub mid-run, and a failed refresh leaves the last good version in place ([#14713](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14713)).
- **Browser Use Cloud, live in the task** — A new Browser Use Cloud connector gives agents governed browser automation, and tasks show interactive browser tabs where people can follow along, take over the page, and keep the browser after the run finishes, with costs recorded against the run ([#14627](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14627)).
- **Connections set up in one click** — Connector setup collapses to one screen that states its defaults and tucks the rest behind "Change" and the Permissions tab ([#14811](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14811)). The Zapier, Arcade, Composio Connect, and Executor MCP aggregators are on by default with the experimental toggle removed ([#13964](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/13964)), and they can be configured from inline task cards ([#13879](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/13879)). Connection search prefers native apps, asks the user to choose an external provider before setup ([#13941](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/13941)), and understands natural-language queries ([#14725](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14725)). New in the catalog: Fireflies with summary-ready routines ([#13890](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/13890)), five experimental memory providers (Mem0, Zep, Supermemory, Cognee, Honcho) behind the default-off `enableMemoryConnectors` setting, plus assigned MCP tools delivered to remote native Codex ([#13942](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/13942)), and GitHub Code Review Bot as its own card separate from GitHub tools ([#14750](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14750)). Personal pasted credentials are validated the same way at setup, health check, and invocation, and new connections request the write scopes their actions need ([#14739](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14739)).
- **Slack goes both ways** — Replies entered on the board reach the linked Slack thread and resume the same conversation, and assigned agents get their Slack tools during ordinary tasks and scheduled routines ([#13920](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/13920)). Slack-origin tasks get governed tools to read the surrounding discussion, create follow-ups, and collaborate through the inviting bot ([#13828](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/13828)), and an answered conversation settles to Idle instead of lingering In Progress ([#13809](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/13809)).
- **Agent Chat grows up** — A secondary chat sidebar and landing page give conversations their own home ([#14706](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14706)); tasks delegated from a chat durably deliver their completion back to it ([#14408](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14408)); a clear approval typed in chat resolves the pending card, and unanswered questions move into history where they can be answered later ([#14613](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14613)); and a chat continues after its native worker is lost ([#13813](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/13813)).
- **A composer that picks the run** — The task composer gains a per-message model and effort picker that follows the selected agent, keeps pending cards visible above it, and works on mobile ([#14322](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14322)); effort options match what each adapter actually executes, including Codex on the native runner ([#14568](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14568), [#14576](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14576)). Tasks can be created from a prompt alone and the assigned agent names them ([#14761](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14761)). Artifacts get rich cards with previews ([#14469](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14469)), an image and video gallery with full-row links ([#13825](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/13825)), and Markdown and text attachments open in task tabs with rendered, raw, and download views ([#14297](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14297)).
- **Governed API tools, on by default** — The native runner's `search_api` and `call_api` tools are enabled without an environment variable ([#14186](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14186)); large API responses stream to disk up to 1 GiB and saved text is readable in bounded pages ([#14301](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14301)); and when an assigned app catalog pushes the tool contract past its limit, agents still reach those tools through search and call ([#14218](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14218)).

## Fixes

- **Native runner and sessions** — Tool outcomes survive shutdown and restart instead of recording a false failure ([#14734](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14734)); failed warm sessions are retired before their sandbox stops ([#14747](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14747)) and recovered cleanup honors the run's terminal outcome ([#14767](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14767)); switching a task to a warm lifecycle acquires a reusable lease ([#14187](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14187)); the OpenCode event stream stays open across turns ([#14582](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14582)) and delivers its shutdown settlement ([#14668](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14668)); Codex account notifications no longer abort a turn ([#13902](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/13902)); Claude and Codex quota exhaustion is classified for the proper backoff ([#13831](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/13831), [#13945](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/13945)); ACP terminal failures keep their redacted provider diagnostics ([#14573](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14573)) and identity guards name the failed check ([#14481](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14481)); the native journal read limit is 256 MiB everywhere ([#14711](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14711)); pending finalization of an accepted result is protected from the stale-lock sweep ([#14219](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14219)); adapters expose a verified provider stop before workspace restoration ([#14311](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14311)); warm sessions keep running under managed GitHub access ([#13815](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/13815)); and a run that hits a provider authentication failure offers an inline connection card in the task so the user can repair and continue ([#14629](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14629)).
- **Sandboxes and workspaces** — Daytona commands stay alive after the log socket closes ([#14799](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14799)), confirmed container loss is recognized when resuming leases ([1f3ff75d](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/commit/1f3ff75d334ddfbb06d49c1033ec2b89be594e20)), failed allocations are cleaned up ([#13979](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/13979)), and provider acquisition timeouts honor the driver's default ([#14097](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14097)). ACP input delivery retries after a gateway 502 without duplicating input ([#14485](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14485)), oversized launch payloads and duplicated wake context no longer fail with `E2BIG` ([#13793](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/13793), [#13891](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/13891)), process proxies close after remote exit ([#13777](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/13777)), and relative symlinks in secondary repositories are preserved ([#13953](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/13953)). Workspace exports finalize and recover safely ([#14402](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14402)), restore failures keep the adapter's result and record what failed ([#14035](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14035), [#14064](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14064)), large Git snapshots stream through disk manifests instead of hitting a 1 MiB output limit ([#14194](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14194), [#14253](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14253)), readiness checks accept larger status output ([#14414](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14414)), background scans stop refreshing the Git index ([#14666](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14666)), partial task overrides retain project setup commands ([#14502](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14502)), and repository-free low-trust tasks get a private directory ([#14766](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14766)).
- **Scheduler and recovery** — A queued run whose claim is permanently rejected is cancelled instead of crash-looping the server ([#14738](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14738)); wakes that arrive during a drain stay queued and interrupted corrective runs get a transient retry ([#14028](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14028)); an issue whose run has spent its retry budget is escalated to a visible blocked state rather than skipped forever ([#14046](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14046)); continuation and retry budgets use persisted state ([#13888](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/13888)); task ownership is claimed atomically with queued runs ([#13973](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/13973)); obsolete continuations are cancelled before dispatch ([#13761](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/13761)); a status reply that still lists blocking work keeps the task moving ([#14626](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14626)); Done and Cancelled tasks keep their assignee on release ([#14561](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14561)); interaction continuations stay scoped to their task ([ded156a9](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/commit/ded156a9045d59cf8705847271c8c03b1b58c8b2)) and question recipients are derived and validated ([#14742](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14742)); Slack- and Discord-origin tasks that lose their review path recover with their message bindings intact instead of failing the recovery authorization check ([#13818](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/13818)); remote Grok runs stop before queued messages continue ([#14100](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14100)); run-identity locks no longer deadlock with audit inserts ([#14478](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14478)); and ambiguous database disconnects are no longer replayed ([#14773](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14773)).
- **Connections and apps** — OAuth sign-in challenges and reconnect states return 422 instead of being reported as crashes ([#13786](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/13786), [#13794](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/13794)); MCP OAuth setup explains failed or cancelled consent ([#13855](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/13855)); a disabled Slack MCP app gets actionable setup instructions ([a7d3b17a](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/commit/a7d3b17a970a305e9b2cc2bebc2b16950e8bd31f)); broker and AgentMail failures keep allowlisted reason codes ([#14098](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14098), [#14768](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14768)); Google Chat and the Docs, Sheets, Slides, and Calendar profiles request fewer scopes ([#13820](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/13820), [#14740](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14740)); work products validate their execution-workspace reference ([#14063](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14063)); and malformed CLI auth challenge IDs return 400 ([#14095](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14095)).
- **Board UI** — The board recovers during server restarts with a connection message and retries, keeping open editors mounted ([#14560](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14560)), and offers a retry screen when the app fails before React starts ([#13970](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/13970)). Code highlighting no longer crashes on a Lezer version mismatch ([a3749aac](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/commit/a3749aac4680a901fa0fe1cc898907887abc9908)), destructive confirm buttons are readable in the light theme ([#14328](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14328)), mobile pickers stay in view above the keyboard and scroll by touch ([#14022](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14022), [#14249](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14249), [#14250](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14250), [#14599](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14599)), newer drafts survive receipt cleanup ([#14332](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14332)), other users' failed runs stay out of Mine ([#14572](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14572)), "Recovery needed" is distinguished from "Recovery in progress" ([#14326](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14326)) and a misleading Retry no longer appears when recovery is blocked ([#13775](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/13775)), new artifacts register a tab without opening the panel ([#14193](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14193)), the Tasks panel shows ancestors ([#13823](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/13823)), and task content appears sooner with parallel server reads ([#14727](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14727)). Also: property icons align with avatars ([#13319](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/13319)), runner commentary aligns with replies ([#14716](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14716)), project save indicators stack below their label ([#14765](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14765)), archiving a company navigates away ([#13846](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/13846)), experimental settings are alphabetized with empty groups hidden ([#13905](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/13905)), and the Cursor adapter picks the real error over a trace notice ([#14636](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14636)).
- **Observability** — Browser errors carry `SENTRY_ENVIRONMENT` ([#13784](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/13784)) and bounded component context ([#13904](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/13904)); run errors are isolated from later exceptions and a runtime capability header is redacted ([#13826](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/13826)); and run failure reports retain exit details, stacks, causes, runtime activity, and restore classification ([#14575](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14575), [#14585](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14585), [#14665](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14665), [#14639](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14639), [#14787](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14787)).

## Improvements

- The account menu drops its profile rows for a header link and gains an Invite shortcut ([#14480](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14480)); plugins can supply an organization switcher ([#13832](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/13832), [#13854](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/13854)); `PAPERCLIP_HIDDEN_SETTINGS` accepts a wildcard with named exceptions so new experimental flags stay hidden automatically ([#13980](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/13980)) and a `workspaces.isolation` key hides isolation controls ([#13907](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/13907)); the native runner gains a shared rich-ACP transport foundation for upcoming Cursor, GitHub Copilot, and Pi providers ([#14430](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14430)); native agents can hire teammates through a governed `hire_agent` action that inherits the caller's runtime configuration from a closed allowlist ([#13852](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/13852)); the coordination skill no longer tells agents to escalate through managers instead of asking the human who can act ([#14188](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14188)); worktree seed-source failures explain the supported setups ([#14795](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14795)); Google Workspace connectors are temporarily hidden from the Connections page while Google OAuth verification is pending, with saved connections and runtime access untouched ([#14774](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14774)); and the README is refreshed with current harnesses, guide links, and an npx-first Quickstart ([#14741](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14741), [#14744](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14744)).

## Upgrade Guide

- **Migrations `0284`–`0293`** run on upgrade: `0284` adds and `0289` drops the per-user `keyboard_shortcuts` column; `0285` widens `assets.byte_size` to `bigint`; `0286` adds API response capture reservations; `0287` adds agent instruction heads, revisions, and working copies for persistent agent files; `0288` adds chat completion deliveries and task handoffs; `0290` adds Browser Use Cloud sessions, runs, and browsers; `0291`–`0292` add company skill sources and entries, and `0291` also adopts existing skills imported from `github.com` into them (one source per repository and tracking ref, one entry per skill, and `legacySkillSourceId` / `skillSourcePath` stamped into each skill's metadata; skills imported from GitHub Enterprise hosts, bundled skills, and catalog skills are left as they are, and no provider requests or content rewrites happen); `0293` adds `issues.title_needs_generation`.
- **Operator UI snippets are removed** ([#13789](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/13789)): `PAPERCLIP_CLOUD_UI_SNIPPET` and `PAPERCLIP_CLOUD_UI_SNIPPET_B64` are ignored. Move the integration to a plugin UI contribution before upgrading.
- **Keyboard shortcut settings are removed** ([#14643](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14643)): drop any automation that calls `/api/auth/preferences` or sends `keyboardShortcuts` to the general settings route.
- **Agent mentions no longer dispatch** ([#14577](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14577)): use assignment or a review request to bring another agent onto a task.
- **New defaults**: the native runner's API tools are enabled unless `PAPERCLIP_RUNNER_API_TOOLS_ENABLED` is set to anything other than `true`; `PAPERCLIP_RUNNER_API_TOOLS_COMPANY_IDS` still narrows them ([#14186](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14186)). The MCP aggregators are available without the former `enableMcpAggregators` flag ([#13964](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/13964)).
- **New environment variables**, all optional: `PAPERCLIP_RUNNER_API_COMPANY_CAPTURE_MAX_BYTES` caps captured API response bytes per company (default 20 GiB, minimum 1 GiB; [#14301](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14301)); `PAPERCLIP_WORKSPACE_GIT_SNAPSHOT_TIMEOUT_MS` bounds workspace snapshot time (default 30 minutes, maximum 24 hours) and `PAPERCLIP_WORKSPACE_MANIFEST_MIN_FREE_BYTES` sets the free-disk reserve for snapshot manifests (default 256 MiB, minimum 64 MiB; [#14253](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14253)). Codex ACP runs accept `CODEX_API_KEY` as an alternative to `OPENAI_API_KEY` ([#14322](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14322)).
- **Harness pins moved** to Codex 0.156.0, Claude Agent SDK 0.3.280, and OpenCode 1.18.32 ([#13838](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/13838)); shared installations should refresh their provider CLIs to match.
- No other configuration or API changes require action.

## Contributors

This release has 179 commits from 7 contributors. Thank you to everyone who contributed to this release!

@MrBlackTongue, @gentslava

name: v2026.1001.0
body:
# Paperclip v2026.1001.0

> Released: 2026-10-01

Paperclip v2026.1001.0 carries 77 commits, promoted from `2026.921.0-beta.1`. The headline is reliability: a deep hardening pass over the native runner and chat recovery — approval and Stop races, session continuity, sandbox reconnection and cleanup — alongside a friendlier face: agent personas throughout the app, an animated onboarding character, and a rebuilt Slack setup. Around those: agents can review GitHub pull requests as scheduled review bots, Railway joins the connector catalog with governed deployment tools, approvals and answers queue during active runs instead of bouncing, and execution harnesses now default to full auto.

## Breaking Changes

- **The legacy Composio broker is retired.** The API-key catalog method, broker clients, session creation, account synchronization, child lifecycle and toolkit routes, and the Services tab are all removed. Existing legacy Composio connections stop working, and there is no automated migration — the experimental MCP aggregator connectors (below) are the successor path; see the Upgrade Guide for the manual steps. Vercel provenance is untouched. ([#13758](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/13758))
- **Execution harnesses now default to full auto.** Native runs default Claude/ACPX to `approve-all`, OpenCode to `allow`, and Codex to approval-and-sandbox bypass, and the legacy adapters follow the same policy — provider tools and connected tools included. Explicitly configured restrictive modes are preserved, and Paperclip's own approval decisions still enforce controller authority; only the *defaults* change. Operators who relied on unconfigured agents inheriting restrictive provider gates should set an explicit mode. ([#13686](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/13686), [#13693](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/13693))

## Highlights

- **Agents get faces** — Static persona images replace agent icons across lists, the sidebar, org charts, tasks, comments, selectors, activity, and dashboards, with one animated pointer-following character in the agent header (reduced-motion and touch fallbacks included) and persona reveal built into agent creation ([#13171](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/13171)). Onboarding opens with the ClipLab sleepy-to-wake hero: the character dozes in gray through setup and wakes in full palette on Review ([#13629](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/13629)). Slack setup can download the agent's avatar as a PNG for the bot identity, from both setup and settings ([#13740](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/13740)).
- **Agents review your pull requests** — A guided setup turns a Paperclip agent into a GitHub review bot: a copyable Claude/Codex prompt walks through App installation, review scheduling, and optional required checks, with the instance origin baked in ([#13717](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/13717)). The GitHub MCP connection also gains the Actions toolset — workflow discovery and dispatch — for existing and new connections ([#13553](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/13553)).
- **Approvals and answers queue during active runs** — Responding to a question or approval while the agent is mid-run no longer bounces: resolved cards project into the run queue as immutable responses, an explicit click steers a response into a compatible native turn (or interrupts for a fresh session), and typed context survives interruption and cleanup ([#13539](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/13539)).
